note: HER2-amplified cell lines and BT-474 xenografts carried trastuzumab to the clinic and later set ADC doses; patient biopsies did not show the cell-line mechanism and no animal flagged the heart.
label: Breast cancer (HER2)

engagement.note: Murine 4D5, trastuzumab's parent, bound HER2 and inhibited growth of HER2-overexpressing breast lines such as SK-BR-3.
engagement.quote: a monoclonal antibody directed against the extracellular domain of p185HER2 specifically inhibits the growth of breast tumor-derived cell lines overexpressing the HER2/c-erbB-2 gene product

engagement.note: With tumours saturated by trastuzumab, 11 patients showed no HER2 down-modulation or proliferation change; responders had more ADCC.
engagement.short: No HER2 down-modulation in patient tumours
engagement.quote: The results of this pilot study argue against trastuzumab activity in patients through down-modulation of HER2 but in favor of antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity
engagement.judgement: Binding itself held (saturating tumour trastuzumab in all 11 patients), so the call turns on the model's proximal readout: cell lines predicted HER2 down-modulation and cytostasis, the labelled 'inhibits proliferation' mechanism, and neither appeared in patient tumours. Mohsin 2005 (doi 10.1200/JCO.2005.00.661, n=35) likewise saw no change in total or p-HER2, though apoptosis rose 35%. The TKI arm matched: lapatinib inhibited p-ErbB2/p-Erk/p-Akt in patient biopsies as in BT-474 cells (Spector 2005, doi 10.1200/JCO.2005.12.157), but contra overrides so no entry is drawn. A reviewer who counts receptor saturation as engagement would flip this to same. Abstract-level reading; pilot n=11.

dose.note: Trastuzumab shrank BT-474 xenografts dose-dependently; the clinical trough target was set from such models without a published exposure check.
dose.quote: Treatment of well established BT-474 breast cancer xenografts overexpressing HER2 in athymic mice with rhuMAb HER2 resulted in a dose-dependent antitumor activity.

dose.note: T-DM1 xenograft growth curves gave a tumour-static concentration whose projected human dose range matched the clinical doses.
dose.quote: The accuracy of projected efficacious dose range for T-DM1 was verified by comparison with the clinical doses.
dose.judgement: Retrospective third-party (Pfizer) PK/PD translation of published T-DM1 xenograft data to the clinical dose, not the developer's own projection; the abstract says the projection was verified against clinical doses but gives no fold-difference, so magnitude is left null. Trastuzumab's own trough target (set from preclinical models for the 1996 phase II) never had a published model-vs-patient exposure comparison that I found. Abstract-level; paywalled.

efficacy.note: Paclitaxel plus trastuzumab gave the most complete regressions of BT-474 xenografts; the pivotal trial was built on it.
efficacy.quote: The combination of paclitaxel and rhuMAb HER2 resulted in the highest tumor growth inhibition and had a significantly superior complete tumor regression rate when compared with either paclitaxel or rhuMAb HER2 alone.

efficacy.note: Adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy raised response from 32% to 50% and median survival from 20.3 to 25.1 months.
efficacy.quote: The addition of trastuzumab to chemotherapy was associated with a longer time to disease progression (median, 7.4 vs. 4.6 months; P<0.001), a higher rate of objective response (50 percent vs. 32 percent, P<0.001)
efficacy.judgement: Direction matched; magnitude did not (complete regressions in mice vs an 18-point response gain and 4.8-month survival gain), so direction_only. Trial paper, not a side-by-side comparison. Earlier monotherapy phase II (Baselga 1996, doi 10.1200/JCO.1996.14.3.737; ORR 11.6%) already matched the cell-line growth-inhibition prediction in direction. No published case of this model flagging a HER2 drug that then failed, so neg is not reachable; afatinib (LUX-Breast 1) and adjuvant lapatinib (ALTTO) under-performed trastuzumab but no model-vs-patient comparison was published, so not scored.

safety.note: Trastuzumab does not bind mouse ErbB2, so xenografts were blind to on-target toxicity; monkey toxicology reported none.
safety.quote: Treatment of well established BT-474 breast cancer xenografts overexpressing HER2 in athymic mice with rhuMAb HER2 resulted in a dose-dependent antitumor activity.

safety.note: NYHA class III/IV cardiac dysfunction in 27% on anthracycline plus trastuzumab; no animal study had flagged the heart.
safety.quote: The most important adverse event was cardiac dysfunction of New York Heart Association class III or IV, which occurred in 27 percent of the group given an anthracycline, cyclophosphamide, and trastuzumab
safety.judgement: Patient half is solid (pivotal trial; the seven-trial cardiac review, Seidman 2002, doi 10.1200/JCO.2002.20.5.1215, gives the same 27%). The 'model silent' half rests on the BLA toxicology package (cynomolgus, the only trastuzumab-reactive species), which I did not fetch; the trial abstract does not itself state that animals were silent, hence comparison_stated false. The mechanism was explained only afterwards by ventricle-restricted ErbB2-knockout mice (Crone 2002), a model built after the clinical signal. Tucatinib's HER2-over-EGFR selectivity later predicting less diarrhoea is a matched safety call but contra overrides, so it is not entered.
